dedupe_keys.name: global reservoir and dam database grand

description: GRanD is a global geographically explicit database of large reservoirs and their dams, produced by the Global Water System Project, which collated existing dam and reservoir datasets through eleven participating institutions to give the scientific community a single reliable source; McGill University manages it. Version 1.1 holds 6,862 reservoirs and associated dams with a cumulative storage of 6,197 cubic kilometres; version 1.3 adds 458 records, mostly built between 2000 and 2016, for 7,320 in total, adds 666.5 cubic kilometres of storage, updates attributes and adds a column showing whether and when a dam was removed. Dams are points and reservoirs are polygons delineated from satellite imagery, with attributes such as names, river, construction year, dam dimensions, reservoir area and capacity and main use. Coverage is global. Data are available from the Global Dam Watch directory and, for version 1, from NASA Earthdata (former SEDAC collection), free of charge; the licence was not read on the GRanD page. Caveats: GRanD is superseded by the Global Dam Watch consensus database and will not be developed further, it covers large reservoirs only, and version 1.1 remains available for reproducibility. Simulation uses: system description of reservoirs for flood-control, water-supply and irrigation models, river routing, downstream hazard exposure and climate adaptation studies. Its successor is catalogued as data-global-dam-watch-database.
